sections.h2: What does a Westfield seller face between signing and closing?
sections.html:
Three things: a fire department alarm check, a deed filed in Elizabeth and a quarterly tax bill. Westfield asks for no resale certificate of occupancy, and its high price level is the more unusual feature, because the town's typical home value sits just under the million-dollar mark where a surcharge begins.

What follows lays out local figures, the alarm inspection, recording and tax steps, then compares an agent listing, a sale handled alone and an as-is cash purchase.

sections.h2: How big is Westfield and what do homes cost there?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts Westfield at 32,595 people for mid-2025, against 31,032 counted in 2020. The land area is 6.72 square miles, giving about 4,615 residents for each square mile, and roughly four of every five homes are occupied by the people who own them.

A suburb like this draws buyers who compare it with Cranford, Scotch Plains and Mountainside. For pricing, the most useful evidence is a handful of recent closings close to your own address.

sections.h2: How do Westfield's old village, downtown and schools shape demand?
sections.html:
Settlers arrived in the area in 1720, the place became a separate township in January 1794, and it took its present form as a town in 1903. The shopping district north of the station is run through a special improvement district by the Downtown Westfield Corporation and, per Wikipedia, holds over 200 retail businesses.

The railroad also divides the town into a North Side and a South Side, and the school system follows that line. Westfield Public Schools enrolled 5,979 students across ten buildings in 2023-24:

  • Lincoln Early Childhood Center for pre-kindergarten and kindergarten;
  • six elementary schools, three on each side of the tracks;
  • Roosevelt Intermediate in the north and Edison Intermediate in the south;
  • Westfield High School, with 1,784 students.

Green space helps too. Mindowaskin Park and Tamaques Park lie inside town limits, and Lenape Park, at 450 acres, belongs to the Union County Rahway River Parkway.

sections.h2: Why does commuting access matter so much for Westfield prices?
sections.html:
NJ Transit's Raritan Valley Line serves Westfield station, with direct trains into New York Penn Station outside weekday rush hours and some non-stop rush-hour service toward Newark Penn. A bus numbered 113 reaches the Port Authority terminal.

By road, Route 28 follows the tracks for about two miles. Garden State Parkway Exits 135 and 137 and the Route 22 ramps at Lawrence, Mountain and Springfield Avenues lie a short distance away. The town has 108.63 miles of roadway, and the municipality maintains 96.69 of them.

Offer the walk time to the platform and the drive to the nearest ramp when you describe the house. Commuters weigh those two numbers heavily.

sections.h2: Does a Westfield sale need a certificate of occupancy?
sections.html:
It does not. The Westfield building department states the town requires no certificate of occupancy or continued certificate of occupancy for a home sale. What it does require is a Certificate of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance.

State fire safety law makes the owner of a one- or two-family house obtain that paper from the Bureau of Fire Prevention before the buyer takes over, and a failure to do so brings a $200 fine. Points sellers raise most often:

  • Crews inspect on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, without a phone call about the arrival time.
  • The price depends on lead time: $100 for a slot more than ten business days out, $125 for four to ten, $150 for under four.
  • Someone aged 18 or over has to let the crew in, because they will not enter an empty house alone.
  • Sealed ten-year battery alarms pass, and so do hardwired detectors.
  • Any open construction permit has to be closed first.
  • Since March 14, 2025 the fire extinguisher is no longer part of the check.

The certificate arrives by email at the single address given on the application, so use the one belonging to your closing attorney or agent. A house headed for demolition still needs one.

sections.h2: Where does a Westfield deed get recorded, and what does the state charge?
sections.html:
Union County records the deed at the County Clerk's courthouse office, 2 Broad Street, Elizabeth. Over-the-counter filing runs until 3:30 in the afternoon, and no appointment is needed. A second clerk's office in Westfield, on North Avenue East, covers passports, notary commissions and trade names, so deeds still go to Elizabeth.

The seller owes the state's realty transfer fee. Above a $350,000 price the schedule starts at $2.90 for each $500 of the first $150,000, climbs to $4.25 through $200,000, and then charges $4.80 until $550,000, with $5.30 and $5.80 tiers above that. Westfield's typical value of $953,400 falls in the $5.30 tier.

Residential sales over $1,000,000 also draw the Graduated Percent Fee, 1 percent of the whole price up to $2,000,000. On a $1,050,000 sale, that is about $10,500, so have the closing attorney run the arithmetic before you accept an offer near the threshold.

sections.h2: How are Westfield property taxes billed around a sale?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector at 425 E Broad Street bills four times a year, on the first of February, May, August and November, and extends each deadline by ten calendar days. If the tenth lands on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies.

Interest on late payments is 8 percent of the first $1,500 and 18 percent of anything beyond, reaching back to the original due date, and a bounced check adds $20. Sewer fees come on a different cycle, due April 1. The office tells new owners to request a bill because an unreceived bill does not excuse payment, so ask for a written payoff of tax and sewer before closing and let the closing agent split the current quarter.

Senior and veteran relief applications also pass through this office, so confirm any deduction on the account is settled.

sections.h2: Which Westfield path suits you: agent, solo sale or cash buyer?
sections.html:
An agent listing generally reaches the most buyers, a cash purchase closes fastest, and a solo sale saves the commission at the cost of doing all the work. Condition and timing usually decide it.

  • Choose an agent when the house shows well and you can sit through open houses, buyer inspections and mortgage underwriting.
  • Handle it alone when you know your block's recent sales and will pay an attorney to prepare the contract.
  • Choose an as-is cash buyer for an inherited house, a tenant in place, or repairs you would rather not make before moving.

Whichever you pick, request a fire department date once a closing date is penciled in, since only two mornings a week are available. Compare written offers by the amount left after the transfer fee, any surcharge above $1,000,000, taxes and the loan payoff.

faqs.q: What costs come with selling a Westfield house?
faqs.a: The seller pays the state realty transfer fee, which follows the price, plus a fire department inspection of $100 to $150. Sales above $1,000,000 add a 1 percent surcharge. A listing agent's commission, if you use one, is separate.

faqs.q: Is an inspection needed before closing in Westfield?
faqs.a: Yes, an alarm and carbon monoxide inspection by the Bureau of Fire Prevention. The building department says no certificate of occupancy is needed. Crews come on Tuesday and Thursday mornings.

faqs.q: What are the Westfield tax installments?
faqs.a: Four bills fall due on the first of February, May, August and November, each with a ten-day cushion. Sewer is separate and due April 1. Late interest is 8 percent up to $1,500 and 18 percent beyond.

faqs.q: Can a Westfield house with problems still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The alarm check covers only alarms and detectors, though open permits must be closed. A buyer can take on cosmetic or structural work, which is how as-is purchases function.

faqs.q: Which office files a Westfield deed?
faqs.a: The Union County Clerk in Elizabeth, at 2 Broad Street. Walk-in filing needs no appointment, and your closing attorney or title company normally files it for you.
